# RX Tracker NEXT 4.0.0-next.25

Staging performance candidate dated 2026-07-25.

## What changed

- Call Center queue count, filtering, sorting, and pagination now execute in PostgreSQL before page relationships and history are loaded.
- Called-today and login activity use bounded SQL common-table expressions and page-scoped history.
- Call-attempt analytics use grouped database aggregates for outcomes, ring time, and conversation time.
- Eight additive indexes support Call Center audit history, call chronology, RX workflow history, patient notes, user activity, and error-log chronology.

## Observed staging performance

On the annual stress dataset containing 5,000 patients, 12,000 RX records,
51,420 workflow rows, and 50,000 call attempts:

- Warm 10-patient Call Center page: approximately 1.0-1.2 seconds before, 11-14 ms after.
- Relationship and call-history sorts: approximately 12-23 ms.
- 50,000-attempt report summary: approximately 92-96 ms before, 51-53 ms after.
- The optimized attempt summary returned exactly the same totals and outcome counts as the prior implementation.

## Database impact

One audited additive migration creates eight indexes on existing columns. It
does not alter columns, constraints, patients, RX records, call attempts,
phone accounts, proxy routes, application origins, ports, or RX Softphone.
No business data is rewritten.

The wider growth audit found that DailySnapshots, relay commands, and
service-date histories/cycles already use bounded or adequately indexed access,
so those areas were intentionally left unchanged.

## Validation

- Complete staging smoke suite passed.
- Isolated full browser workflow passed.
- Call Center attempt/lifecycle, queue-reopen, and non-company regressions passed.
- 37 migrations applied with zero pending and verified checksums.
- No high or critical npm audit findings.

This is a staging candidate. Do not install it in production until it is
promoted through develop, built, and published as an official checksummed
release.
